digest.component_or_area: code-review impact model (v3 → v4 redesign) and tests lane routing
propositions: Code-v3 impact model discards verifier-supplied prod_impact and trigger_likelihood fields for maint-lane findings, preventing blocking of test-sufficiency issues with high user reach

A test assertion contradicting a co-shipped contract declaration (stale=0 vs stale>0 allowed) was missed by code-review because tests antipattern matching is refactor-based and does not detect contract-state contradictions

Code-v4 introduces lane-scoped impact multipliers: serious-maint ×1.0 undamped, moderate-maint prod_impact-keyed, debt churn-amplifier-only; consequence lanes only apply reversibility floor; tests threshold moves to 0.54 blocking
Moderate-maint findings now use prod_impact to scale impact (high/med=1.0, low=0.6, none=0.5) and lane-specific trigger maps (rare 0.75, sometimes/common 1.0) to reach blocking thresholds
New forbids_contract_allowed_state binary flags tests forbidding a state the same diff's contract declares allowed, with both-halves verbatim evidence and tightening-intent guard
Replay under code-v4: blocking increases from 42 to 99 changes (3.4% → 8.0%), zero demotions of currently-blocking findings, internal-edge advisory mass preserved
